$comment: Target languages. 'defaultTargets' is used when a request does not name languages. Add entries (e.g. zh-Hans, ja) to extend. 'translator' is the Azure Translator code used for the NMT fallback.

bg.name: Bulgarian
bg.formal: Address the reader with the polite plural (Вие forms).
bg.informal: Address the reader with ти forms.
bg.style: Use „…“ quotation marks and a decimal comma.

cs.name: Czech
cs.style: Use „…“ quotation marks and a decimal comma.

da.name: Danish
da.formal: Use 'du'; it is the standard professional form in Danish ('De' is archaic).

de.name: German
de.style: Use „…“ quotation marks and a decimal comma. Hyphenate compounds with product names or English terms (e.g. 'Azure-Ressource').

el.name: Greek
el.style: Use «…» quotation marks, a decimal comma and ';' as the question mark.

es.name: Spanish (Spain)
es.style: Use opening ¿ and ¡, «…» or "…" quotation marks and a decimal comma.

et.name: Estonian
et.style: Use „…“ quotation marks and a decimal comma.

fi.name: Finnish
fi.formal: Prefer neutral passive or imperative constructions; avoid overly familiar tone.
fi.style: Use ”…” quotation marks and a decimal comma.

fr.name: French (France)
fr.style: Use « … » quotation marks, a non-breaking space before : ; ! ? and a decimal comma.

ga.name: Irish
ga.formal: Use standard Irish (An Caighdeán Oifigiúil) in a professional register; address one reader with 'tú'.
ga.informal: Use standard Irish in a friendly register; address one reader with 'tú'.
ga.style: Keep established English technical terms only where no accepted Irish term exists.

hr.name: Croatian
hr.style: Use „…“ quotation marks and a decimal comma.

hu.name: Hungarian
hu.style: Use „…” quotation marks and a decimal comma.

it.name: Italian
it.style: Use «…» or "…" quotation marks and a decimal comma.

lt.name: Lithuanian
lt.style: Use „…“ quotation marks and a decimal comma.

mt.name: Maltese
mt.style: Use correct Maltese orthography (ċ, ġ, ħ, ż, għ). Prefer established Maltese terms; keep English technical loanwords only where they are standard.

pl.name: Polish
pl.formal: Avoid 'ty'; use impersonal constructions or polite forms.
pl.style: Use „…” quotation marks and a decimal comma.

pt.name: Portuguese (Portugal)
pt.formal: Use formal European Portuguese, third-person address; avoid 'tu'.
pt.style: European Portuguese vocabulary and spelling, never Brazilian (ficheiro, ecrã, utilizador, transferir). Use «…» quotation marks and a decimal comma.

ro.name: Romanian
ro.style: Use ș and ț with comma below (not cedilla), „…” quotation marks and a decimal comma.

sk.name: Slovak
sk.style: Use „…“ quotation marks and a decimal comma.

sl.name: Slovenian
sl.style: Use »…« or „…“ quotation marks and a decimal comma.

sv.name: Swedish
sv.formal: Use 'du'; it is the standard even in formal Swedish ('ni' as polite singular sounds dated).
sv.style: Use ”…” quotation marks, a decimal comma and a space as thousands separator.

nb.name: Norwegian Bokmål
nb.formal: Use 'du'; it is the standard professional form.
nb.style: Use «…» quotation marks and a decimal comma.

uk.name: Ukrainian
uk.style: Use «…» quotation marks and a decimal comma.

zh-Hans.name: Chinese (Simplified)
zh-Hans.formal: Use a neutral, professional register (您 where direct address is needed).
zh-Hans.style: Use full-width Chinese punctuation; keep a space between Chinese and Latin text only where it aids readability.

ja.name: Japanese
ja.informal: Use plain form (だ/である) in a friendly tone.
